messages.workspaces.canEditDetail: Open its files and start tasks on it
messages.workspaces.canViewDetail: Open its files and copy it
messages.workspaces.sharedWith: {count, plural, one {Shared with # person} other {Shared with # people}}
messages.workspaces.name: Name
messages.workspaces.deleteWithTasks: Delete “{name}” and its {count, plural, one {# task} other {# tasks}}? The tasks and the files are removed.
messages.workspaces.deleteWorking: A task is working in “{name}”. It can be deleted once that task is done.
messages.workspaces.deletePinned: “{task}” keeps its environment on, so “{name}” can’t be deleted. Turn off Keep environment on in that task’s ⋯ first.
messages.workspaces.deletePinnedOther: Another task keeps its environment on, so “{name}” can’t be deleted.
messages.workspaces.deleteOthers: Other people have tasks on “{name}”, so it can’t be deleted.
messages.workspaces.deleteNotReady: “{name}” is still being copied. It can be deleted once the copy is finished.
messages.workspaces.deleteRefused: This workspace is in use or has other people’s tasks, so it can’t be deleted now.
messages.workspaces.deleteHasHelpers: This workspace has a task that leads helpers. Delete that task with its helpers first, then delete the workspace.
messages.workspaces.shareIntro: People you add can open its files; with Can edit they can also start their own tasks on it. They never see your tasks.
messages.workspaces.emailInvalid: Enter one email address, not your own.
